review_notes: I read the whole file and concentrated on the Spatial section (lines 178–260). There, `radial_upper_enclosure` and `radial_lower_exterior` repeat the same intermediate-value argument along a ray. The other candidates were short or routine: the repeated `rwa [measure_interior_eq]` lines, the `cases i <;> first | ...` blocks in `pointwise_radial`, and the structural similarity between `diagonal_common_limit` and `actual_radial_comparison`. I did not report those. I did not run Lean, so the proposed helper and the rewrites are untested. In particular, `intermediate_value_Icc` yields a point where the distance equals `h`, and I assume that unifies with `∈ sphere p h` by `Metric.mem_sphere`/definitional unfolding. The existing proofs already pass `heq` straight to `hb`, which supports this.

findings.problem: Both proofs run the same ray-crossing argument. First they derive `Continuous f` from `hs` (lines 215 and 238). Then they build the continuity of `s ↦ dist (f (base + s • v)) p` (lines 216–218 and 239–241). Then they supply the endpoint inequalities `dist (f base) p ≤ h ≤ dist (f (base + t • v)) p` and call `intermediate_value_Icc` to get a parameter `s ∈ Icc 0 t` with `f (base + s • v)` on `sphere p h` (lines 222 and 244). Only the base point (`f.symm x` versus `f.symm p`) and the endpoint `t` (an exit time versus `1`) differ. The topological content, that a ray whose image goes from inside to outside the closed ball must meet the sphere, is written out twice with its own continuity and IVT bookkeeping.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a helper in `PlanarHalving.Spatial` before `radial_upper_enclosure`:

lemma exists_ray_param_on_sphere (f : OpenPartialHomeomorph Point Point) (hs : f.source = univ) (a v p : Point) {h t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (h0 : dist (f a) p ≤ h) (h1 : h ≤ dist (f (a + t • v)) p) : ∃ s ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) t, f (a + s • v) ∈ sphere p h.

Proof sketch: `hf : Continuous f := continuousOn_univ.mp (by simpa only [hs] using f.continuousOn)`. Then `hcont : Continuous fun s : ℝ => dist (f (a + s • v)) p` as in the current code. Rewrite `h0` using `zero_smul, add_zero`. Then `obtain ⟨s, hs', heq⟩ := intermediate_value_Icc ht hcont.continuousOn ⟨h0', h1⟩` and `exact ⟨s, hs', heq⟩`.

Use in `radial_upper_enclosure`: replace lines 215–222 with `obtain ⟨s, hs', heq⟩ := exists_ray_param_on_sphere f hs (f.symm x) v p ht (by simpa only [f.right_inv (hball hx)] using Metric.mem_closedBall.mp hx) (not_le.mp hexit).le`. The rest is unchanged.

Use in `radial_lower_exterior`: replace lines 238–244 with `obtain ⟨s, hs', heq⟩ := exists_ray_param_on_sphere f hs (f.symm p) v p zero_le_one (by simpa [f.right_inv hp] using hh) (by simpa [v, f.right_inv hx] using hxp)`. The remaining lines `hb'`, `rw` and `exact` are unchanged. Both uses keep their current hypotheses (`hs`, `hball`, `hp`, `hh`, `hxp`) and need no new imports.
findings.benefit: The IVT-on-a-ray reasoning and the continuity of `f` along it are stated and proved once, and each enclosure lemma shrinks to the ray-specific computation. The main hypothesis (`f.source = univ`) is then used in one place for continuity, and a future change to the IVT bookkeeping, such as a different sphere or ball convention, needs one edit. A reader can also see that the two lemmas are the inside and outside halves of one argument.
